pick.name: Handy
pick.what: Open-source push-to-talk dictation that transcribes locally and pastes into any app
pick.why: Runs fully offline on this no-GPU laptop with the CPU-optimised Parakeet V3 model, so nothing leaves the company machine; free

alts.name: Windows voice typing (Win+H)
alts.what: Built-in Windows dictation (Azure online speech recognition, India English supported)
alts.why: Zero install; fallback when you cannot install apps (for example on a work laptop); needs internet (cloud processing)

alts.name: Wispr Flow (Free)
alts.what: Cloud AI dictation with formatting, on Windows and Android
alts.why: Best accuracy/formatting and the only one that also covers Android dictation; free cap is the limit
alts.free_limits: Free: 2,000 words/week on desktop, limited mobile; Pro $12/user/mo annual

candidates.name: Handy
candidates.verdict: PICK: local, MIT, CPU model, free

candidates.name: Windows voice typing
candidates.verdict: Built in, but cloud and weaker formatting

candidates.name: Wispr Flow
candidates.verdict: Best polish + Android, 2k words/week free; cloud processing

candidates.name: Vibe
candidates.verdict: MIT offline file transcription with diarization (v3.2.2 2026-09-05); use for recorded voice memos, not live dictation

decision: Handy is the best fit: offline, open source, works without a GPU and costs nothing, which matters on a company-managed laptop. Use Vibe to batch-transcribe voice memos recorded on the phone, and Wispr Flow if you want the same dictation on Android and accept cloud processing.
details: Voice memos on Android: record, then batch-transcribe locally with Vibe.

verify.note: Handy: MIT (brand assets excluded), Windows/macOS/Linux, Parakeet V3 'CPU-optimized', winget cjpais.Handy noted as not maintained by the Handy devs. v0.9.8 date not re-confirmed.
